_README: THE NAMED KNOWN-FLAKE LIST. bin/gate reports entries matched here SEPARATELY from
failures, so that a red OUTSIDE this list is a real red and Task 9's gate clause
'all previous tasks' tests still pass' can be discharged honestly rather than
probabilistically. Before this file existed, three live intermittents meant any new
red could be attributed to one of them by assertion.
RULES FOR THIS FILE, and they are the whole value of it:
- An entry is a NAMED §5 row, its OWNER and its MEASURED rate with the commit and
date it was measured at. No entry without all three. KnownFlakeListTest enforces
it, and also enforces that every 'row' here is a real row in PLAN.md §5.
- Adding an entry is a disposition, not a convenience. A red that is merely
unexplained does NOT belong here -- that is the opposite of this file's purpose.
- An entry is REMOVED when its row is closed, and removing it is how a fix is
proven to have landed. R-200 was removed on 2026-11-01 by being fixed.
- THERE ARE TWO SYMPTOM FAMILIES, NOT ONE PER ROW, and this file says so rather
than listing rows as if they were independent. R-092 predates and is the parent
of both.
MATCHING. 'tests' matches the failing test's class as Pest prints it. 'signature' is
a regex over that failure's own block of output. A family whose identity is a random
test CANNOT be matched by name -- R-191 strikes a different file every time -- so it
is matched by its SQLSTATE and frame, which is exactly what its own row instructs a
reader to check.

flakes.title: 08006 connect timeout on pgsql_owner at TestCase::setUp's TRUNCATE, striking a random test
flakes.rate: 3 of 3 full `composer gate` runs red at a6ece55; 0 of 2 under a bare `php artisan test`. Predecessor R-092 measured 3 red in 10 full-suite runs at 056d7a1 (2026-10-27), 2 of those this family.
identities: MemberConcurrencyTest (stated as a hypothesis, not a cause)
PasskeyTest (2026-11-02 at e761f2c, on pgsql_owner at the TRUNCATE)
PanelProblemPageTest (2026-11-02 at 94f5b5b, on pgsql at a users SELECT -- the symptom that proved the matcher narrower than the cause)
matcher_history: THE FRAME WAS TestCase.php:112 UNTIL 2026-11-02, AND IT HAD BEEN STALE SINCE TASK 9.
This family strikes setUp()'s TRUNCATE, and Task 9 moved that call site from line 112 to
222 (git log -- tests/TestCase.php -> 46e3e52). From that commit on, every R-191 red came
out of bin/classify-reds as a REAL RED. Measured at e761f2c: PasskeyTest failed with
08006/timeout expired on pgsql_owner at TestCase.php:223 and the verdict was REAL RED,
1 of 1 failure(s) are on no row -- for a fault whose own row describes it exactly.
A line-pinned frame goes stale whenever the file moves, and the failure mode is the worst
available: an UNEXPLAINED red, which PLAN 4a calls this project's most expensive defect
shape. The frame now matches the FILE and any line, and the widening is paid for by making
the SIGNATURE carry what this family's own title already says -- pgsql_owner and the
TRUNCATE. The pair is at least as specific as before and no longer depends on a line
number nobody maintains.
NOT a new entry and NOT a new rate: the family, its owner and its measured rate are
untouched. What changed is that the matcher matches the family it was measured for.
KnownFlakeListTest's negative control -- the same SQLSTATE at a DIFFERENT frame must come
out REAL -- is unchanged and still green, and a third fixture pins the stale-line case.
AND THE FIRST REPAIR WAS STILL TOO NARROW -- CORRECTED THE SAME DAY, WITH A FRESH
MEASUREMENT. Pinning pgsql_owner and the TRUNCATE matched the symptom as this row's
TITLE describes it, and the very next full gate run produced the same fault on a
DIFFERENT connection and a different statement: PanelProblemPageTest, 08006 timeout
expired on connection pgsql, on a SELECT of users. Still REAL, still unexplained.
MEASURED AT 94f5b5b, which is what justifies the wider pattern rather than assertion:
full composer gate      2 of 2 RED -- 08006 both times, two different tests, two
different connections, two different statements
bare php artisan test   2 of 2 GREEN -- 1198 passed / 10604 assertions each
That is this row's own recorded rate reproduced at a new commit (a6ece55 gave 3 of 3
red under the gate and 0 of 2 under a bare run), and it says the variable is HOST LOAD
rather than any statement: the gate runs nine steps before the suite.
SO THE MATCHER NOW KEYS ON THE CONNECT PATH, which is what the why_not_a_code_defect
measurement below actually identifies: Connectors/Connector.php is where PDO::connect
is called, and a connect timeout CANNOT be caused by any code in this repository --
only by the host. That is the strongest available argument for a wide pattern, and it
is why this widening is defensible where a bare 08006 would not be.
⚠ AND THE PATTERN CARRIES NO SLASH, WHICH COST ONE ITERATION: bin/classify-reds calls
preg_match('/'.$frame.'/', ...), so a frame of Connectors/Connector\.php was an INVALID
pattern -- the directory separator closed the delimiter -- and preg_match returned false
for every fixture at once. All five came out REAL, including the two that had just been
proven attributed, which is the loud failure rather than the quiet one and is how it was
caught immediately. The file name alone is specific: there is one Connector.php on the
connect path. TestCase.php is kept beside it because r191-attributed.txt is a constructed
fixture from before this project captured a real block and carries no vendor frame.
THE CONTROLS THAT PAY FOR IT, all still green: r191-wrong-frame.txt puts the same
SQLSTATE at app/Features/Pager/PagerSessions.php:204 -- an 08006 raised by a QUERY
rather than by a connect -- and stays REAL; mixed.txt keeps a real red beside an
attributed one and stays REAL; and r191-other-connection.txt is the verbatim capture
of the run described above.
flakes.why_not_a_code_defect: Measured to the host, not argued: 300 bare TCP connects to 127.0.0.1:5432 idle gave 0 failed / median 0.0 ms / max 0.9 ms; the same 300 with eight CPU-spinning threads gave 0 failed / median 162.6 ms / p95 320.1 ms / max 35,648 ms -- a 35-second stall on one connect() with no Postgres in the path. The WSL2 + Docker userspace port forward is the cause. qrpager_owner peaked at 2 backends against a CONNECTION LIMIT of 10, so role limits are not it, and no connect_timeout is configured anywhere.

flakes.title: OutboxWorker::claim() returns ZERO rows where the test expects one, under full-suite load
flakes.rate: 2 failures in roughly 7 full-suite runs on task-8b-precoding (2026-11-01); 8 of 8 green for the file in isolation; the §11 QA round did not reproduce it in 3 full runs at 5f7ffdc. Predecessor R-092 fault two: 1 red in 10 full-suite runs at 056d7a1.
flakes.why_not_a_code_defect: ⚠ UNRESOLVED, AND THAT IS WHY THIS ENTRY IS THE WEAKER OF THE TWO. R-185 exists precisely because R-172's diagnosis is a hypothesis presented as a cause: nothing yet distinguishes 'the test's own fixture races' from 'claim() drops work under load', and the second would be a failure of TASK 4's NAMED INVARIANT rather than a flaky test. Strongly load-correlated (the failing run took 335.53s against a typical ~205s). An entry here attributes the red to a named row; it does NOT certify the row's diagnosis. If this family is ever reproduced in isolation, it leaves this file and becomes a Task 4 defect.

removed.title: PagerPollLatencyTest's exec()'d harness lost its seeded session to the suite
removed.why: FIXED, not deferred. The row named the wrong mechanism -- it said a concurrent test's TRUNCATE, and the harness has run on its own Postgres database (qrpager_poll_proof) since it was written while the suite runs on qrpager_test, so no statement the suite issues can reach its rows. The shared resource was REDIS, which every Postgres database shares: TestCase::setUp's clearPagerProjection() deletes t:*:pager:* and pager:tok:* before every test, and a pager session IS a Redis key. The harness now runs in its own logical databases and under its own prefix. Measured both ways: a loop deleting *pager* from Redis while the harness runs failed 10 of 10 before the change and 0 of 10 after it. PagerPollLatencyTest asserts the isolation property and is proven red by putting the harness back on the suite's keyspace.
